# cato_wf_sub_policy (Resource)

The `cato_wf_sub_policy` resource manages an WAN Firewall sub-policy (a nested policy scoped by a SUB_POLICY_SCOPE rule) together with the cleanup rule the API auto-creates inside it. The Cato API has no updateSubPolicy mutation, so changing `name` or `description` forces resource replacement. Documentation for the underlying API can be found at mutation.policy.wanFirewall.addSubPolicy().

## Example Usage

```terraform
// WAN Firewall sub-policy (a nested policy scoped by a SUB_POLICY_SCOPE rule).
//
// NOTE: The Cato API has no updateSubPolicy mutation, so changing `name` or
// `description` forces replacement, which also removes any rules contained in
// the sub-policy. The scope must set at least one non-ANY match field.

// minimal sub-policy
resource "cato_wf_sub_policy" "minimal" {
  name        = "Branch Sites Sub-Policy"
  description = "Rules that only apply to branch sites"

  at = {
    position = "LAST_IN_POLICY"
  }

  scope = {
    enabled     = true
    source      = { subnet = ["192.0.2.0/24"] }
    destination = {}
  }
}

// Scope tracking is API-managed; omit it from scope.

// full sub-policy with a scoped source and a nested rule owned by it
resource "cato_wf_sub_policy" "full" {
  name        = "Datacenter Sub-Policy"
  description = "Rules scoped to datacenter hosts"

  at = {
    position = "LAST_IN_POLICY"
  }

  scope = {
    enabled = true
    source = {
      subnet = ["10.0.0.0/8"]
    }
    destination = {}
  }
}

// a rule placed inside the "full" sub-policy via sub_policy_id
resource "cato_wf_rule" "in_sub_policy" {
  sub_policy_id = cato_wf_sub_policy.full.id

  // Rules owned by a sub-policy are always positioned before the sub-policy
  // cleanup rule; the `at` position below is required by the schema but the
  // provider anchors the rule inside the sub-policy automatically.
  at = {
    position = "LAST_IN_POLICY"
  }

  rule = {
    name    = "Allow datacenter to internal"
    enabled = true
    action  = "ALLOW"
    source  = {}
    destination = {
      subnet = ["10.1.0.0/16"]
    }
    tracking = {
      event = {
        enabled = true
      }
    }
  }

  depends_on = [cato_wf_sub_policy.full]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `at` (Attributes) Position of the sub-policy scope within the WAN Firewall policy. Changes move the scope rule without replacing the sub-policy. Refresh preserves the last applied placement. When cato_bulk_wf_move_rule owns ordering, keep at unchanged to avoid conflicting moves. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--at))
- `description` (String) Sub-policy description. Changing this forces replacement (no updateSubPolicy API).
- `name` (String) Sub-policy name. Changing this forces replacement (no updateSubPolicy API).
- `scope` (Attributes) Scope of the sub-policy. This is the SUB_POLICY_SCOPE rule that defines when the sub-policy applies. Uses the same parameters as a cato_wf_rule rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope))

### Optional

- `cleanup_rule` (Attributes) The sub-policy's cleanup rule — auto-created by the API with the sub-policy and managed as part of this resource. Omit to keep the API defaults (ALLOW, tracking disabled). Uses the same parameters as a cato_wf_rule rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule))

### Read-Only

- `cleanup_rule_id` (String) ID of the cleanup rule the API auto-created inside the sub-policy.
- `id` (String) Sub-policy ID
- `scope_rule_id` (String) ID of the underlying SUB_POLICY_SCOPE rule.

<a id="nestedatt--at"></a>
### Nested Schema for `at`

Required:

- `position` (String) Position relative to a policy, a section or another rule.

Optional:

- `ref` (String) Identifier of the object relative to which the position is defined.


<a id="nestedatt--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scope`

Required:

- `application` (Attributes) Application traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. Can be an empty object {} to match any application. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--application))
- `destination` (Attributes) Destination traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. Can be an empty object {} to match any destination. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--destination))
- `direction` (String) Define the direction on which the rule is applied (https://api.catonetworks.com/documentation/#definition-WanFirewallDirectionEnum)
- `enabled` (Boolean) Attribute to define rule status (enabled or disabled)
- `source` (Attributes) Source traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. Can be an empty object {} to match any source. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--source))

Optional:

- `active_period` (Attributes) Time period during which the rule is active. Outside this period, the rule is inactive. Times should be in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z'). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--active_period))
- `connection_origin` (String) Connection origin of the traffic (https://api.catonetworks.com/documentation/#definition-ConnectionOriginEnum)
- `country` (Attributes Set) Source country traffic matching criteria. Logical ‘OR’ is applied within the criteria set. Logical ‘AND’ is applied between criteria sets. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--country))
- `device` (Attributes Set) Source Device Profile traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--device))
- `device_attributes` (Attributes) Device attributes matching criteria for the rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--device_attributes))
- `device_os` (List of String) Source device Operating System traffic matching criteria. Logical ‘OR’ is applied within the criteria set. Logical ‘AND’ is applied between criteria sets.(https://api.catonetworks.com/documentation/#definition-OperatingSystem)
- `exceptions` (Attributes Set) The set of exceptions for the rule. Exceptions define when the rule will be ignored and the firewall evaluation will continue with the lower priority rules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--exceptions))
- `schedule` (Attributes) The time period specifying when the rule is enabled, otherwise it is disabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--schedule))
- `service` (Attributes) Destination service traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--service))
- `tracking` (Attributes) Tracking is API-managed on SUB_POLICY_SCOPE rules and must be omitted here — the API rejects user-supplied tracking settings on scoping rules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope--tracking))

Read-Only:

- `action` (String) API-managed action for the SUB_POLICY_SCOPE rule.
- `description` (String) API-managed scope description, synchronized with the sub-policy description.
- `id` (String) ID of the rule
- `name` (String) API-managed scope name, synchronized with the sub-policy name.

<a id="nestedatt--cleanup_rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cleanup_rule`

Required:

- `application` (Attributes) Application traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. Can be an empty object {} to match any application. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--application))
- `destination` (Attributes) Destination traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. Can be an empty object {} to match any destination. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--destination))
- `direction` (String) Define the direction on which the rule is applied (https://api.catonetworks.com/documentation/#definition-WanFirewallDirectionEnum)
- `source` (Attributes) Source traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. Can be an empty object {} to match any source. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--source))

Optional:

- `action` (String) The action applied by the Wan Firewall if the rule is matched (https://api.catonetworks.com/documentation/#definition-WanFirewallActionEnum)
- `active_period` (Attributes) Time period during which the rule is active. Outside this period, the rule is inactive. Times should be in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z'). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--active_period))
- `connection_origin` (String) Connection origin of the traffic (https://api.catonetworks.com/documentation/#definition-ConnectionOriginEnum)
- `country` (Attributes Set) Source country traffic matching criteria. Logical ‘OR’ is applied within the criteria set. Logical ‘AND’ is applied between criteria sets. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--country))
- `description` (String) Description of the rule
- `device` (Attributes Set) Source Device Profile traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--device))
- `device_attributes` (Attributes) Device attributes matching criteria for the rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--device_attributes))
- `device_os` (List of String) Source device Operating System traffic matching criteria. Logical ‘OR’ is applied within the criteria set. Logical ‘AND’ is applied between criteria sets.(https://api.catonetworks.com/documentation/#definition-OperatingSystem)
- `enabled` (Boolean) Attribute to define rule status (enabled or disabled)
- `exceptions` (Attributes Set) The set of exceptions for the rule. Exceptions define when the rule will be ignored and the firewall evaluation will continue with the lower priority rules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--exceptions))
- `name` (String) Cleanup rule name. Defaults to the API-generated "<sub-policy name> - Cleanup Rule"; set to rename the cleanup rule.
- `schedule` (Attributes) The time period specifying when the rule is enabled, otherwise it is disabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--schedule))
- `service` (Attributes) Destination service traffic matching criteria. Logical 'OR' is applied within the criteria set. Logical 'AND' is applied between criteria sets. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--service))
- `tracking` (Attributes) Tracking for the cleanup rule. Optional — the API default is disabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--tracking))

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) ID of the rule

<a id="nestedatt--cleanup_rule--application"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cleanup_rule.application`

Optional:

- `app_category` (Attributes Set) Cato category of applications which are dynamically updated by Cato (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--application--app_category))
- `application` (Attributes Set) Applications for the rule (pre-defined) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--application--application))
- `custom_app` (Attributes Set) Custom (user-defined) applications (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--application--custom_app))
- `custom_category` (Attributes Set) Custom Categories – Groups of objects such as predefined and custom applications, predefined and custom services, domains, FQDNs etc. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--application--custom_category))
- `domain` (List of String) A Second-Level Domain (SLD). It matches all Top-Level Domains (TLD), and subdomains that include the Domain. Example: example.com.
- `fqdn` (List of String) An exact match of the fully qualified domain (FQDN). Example: www.my.example.com.
- `global_ip_range` (Attributes Set) Globally defined IP range, IP and subnet objects. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--application--global_ip_range))
- `ip` (List of String) IPv4 addresses
- `ip_range` (Attributes List) A range of IPs. Every IP within the range will be matched (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--application--ip_range))
- `sanctioned_apps_category` (Attributes Set) Sanctioned Cloud Applications - apps that are approved and generally represent an understood and acceptable level of risk in your organization. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cleanup_rule--application--sanctioned_apps_category))
- `subnet` (List of String) Network subnets in CIDR notation

### Nested Schema for `cleanup_rule.active_period`

Optional:

- `effective_from` (String) The time the rule becomes active (RFC3339 format, e.g., '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'). If not specified, the rule is active from creation.
- `expires_at` (String) The time the rule expires and becomes inactive (RFC3339 format, e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z'). If not specified, the rule never expires.

Read-Only:

- `use_expires_at` (Boolean) Whether to use the expires_at time. Computed from the presence of expires_at field.
